Ordinary ticket/transport failures isolate, dependent work defers, normalized provider failures feed a bounded breaker, and shared safety/persistence/ownership/config failures abort with exact prior-success accounting.

Newly proven reachable failures: (1) three immutable-ID lookup HTTP 500s currently advance confirmed-404 grace and retire a live/moved binding; (2) failure after retired-file persistence but before live-store save reloads the same key as both live and retired; (3) corrupt retired state erases the only durable tombstone and permits recreation; (4) semantically identical raw/domain HTTP 500s currently receive different pass/ticket scopes; (5) final lifecycle persistence failure currently logs and reports normal completion.

Preserved hard-won behavior: snapshot omission is never deletion; only bounded direct-GET 404s advance grace; fair oldest-first probe budgeting and shared 200 observation; confirmed-deletion no-resurrection; immutable-ID re-key; create write-ahead and index-lag recovery; full read-only census before lifecycle change; independent ticket failure isolation with dependent-link defer; exact fail-loud aggregate and no fictional Jira rollback. Explicitly inverted behavior is enumerated in the brief, including fail-open legacy stores/tombstone corruption and exception-class-dependent failure scope.

Focused evidence: 32 historical lifecycle/apply/recovery tests passed; 24 persistence/corruption/fail-loud tests passed. Narrow probes established incomplete Protocol acceptance, tombstone loss on corrupt state, erroneous retirement after by-ID 500s, split-brain retirement persistence, and exception-scope divergence. Prior-art citations include current Sentry, GitLab, controller-runtime, Crossplane runtime, HTTPX, and Atlassian bulk result patterns.

Migration/rollback: expand/contract via complete adapter + contract suite, single-observation shadow planning, allowlisted intentional deltas only, mutually exclusive typed write cutover, and compatibility-floor rollback that recognizes/recover/refuses any transaction journal/version. Never dual-write and never delete already-created Jira issues as rollback.

Maintainer decisions remaining: D1 exact breaker rule (recommended: exhausted global 429 immediately; timeout/connect/5xx after 3 consecutive exhausted operations across >=2 tickets; success resets; 401 aborts); D2 after Jira create succeeds but returned-key persistence fails, one bounded idempotent marker/property containment attempt using the known key, then safety-abort/report; D3 no production duck fallback, at most one explicit compatibility-floor adapter if a real external consumer warrants it; D4 additive versioned `lifecycle_intents`/ticket disposition in preview/manifests while preserving current remote-mutation hash/shape during shadowing; D5 RP-02 transaction first and RP-04 snapshot contract agreed before RP-03 write cutover, while observer/shadow work may precede cutover.

RP-06 preliminary behavioral probe complete (main-agent path; independent RP-06 review still pending). Artifact: `.joe-janitor/rp06-pass1-kernel-probe.py`; command: `rtk env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python .joe-janitor/rp06-pass1-kernel-probe.py`; result: `SUMMARY 3/3 current routing divergences reproduced`.

Observed against audited tree `b0aac2314b63fc937b3f1d7d638a97609782e954`: (1) a project code-review LLM criterion with effective `applies_to: ["src/**"]` was appended to Round A and invoked for a synthetic docs-only change because `_activated_code_review_project_criteria`/`CodeReviewBatchRunner` do not apply changed-file routing; (2) a project overlay disabled built-in `docs` in `effective_criteria`, but `glob_triggered_overlays(["docs/readme.md"])` still scheduled it because `applies_to_globs` and `OVERLAY_IDS` read packaged policy; (3) an activated project `exec: DET` criterion and selector appeared in `effective_criteria/effective_routing`, but `det_criteria()` omitted it because the detector consumer reads packaged `routing_index()` with no repository snapshot.

Historical intent makes these explicit deltas, not incidental refactors. `deck-golem-scuff` / ADR 0017 require both gates to consume one effective overlay authority; `daily-syrup-belief` / ADR 0016 require activated project DET invariants in both gates. Conversely the later project-LLM runtime work deliberately pinned unconditional, exactly-once Round-A fan-in, so applying project routing predicates is a behavior change approved by the recovered RP-06 refinement and must be named in its implementation story. The prior exactly-once invariant remains: one selected criterion executes once, but non-applicable/disabled criteria execute zero times with provenance.

Focused current suites remain green despite the reproduced gaps: `tests/unit/test_unified_criteria.py`, `test_code_review_project_criteria.py`, `test_det_invariants.py`, `workflow/test_code_review_workflow.py`, and `test_code_review_ws5.py` => `103 passed in 39.60s`. The existing project-DET code-review test only proves the DET criterion stays outside the LLM fan-in and mocks detector output empty; it does not assert that the effective project detector is selected. This is a concrete test-sourced probe gap for RP-06. No production or tracked file changed.

comments.body:
RP-06 chronology/failure checkpoint update (research-only; no tracked or production changes).

Authority correction: `crabbed-abstract-hapuka` (`761e-5af2-ed57-408a`) and commit `5a56202747` prove that today's unconditional, exactly-once Round-A fan-in for activated project LLM criteria was deliberate. However, the later 2026-08-16 RP-06 proposal immediately preceding the maintainer's `Approved` explicitly classified that behavior as an accidental semantic mismatch and assigned standard applicability plus inclusion/exclusion provenance to the shared Pass-1 framework (`.joe-janitor/raw-chat-2026-08-16.md:7980-8143`; recovered report `:438-476,657-683`). Therefore the approved end state supersedes the older behavior: an activated project criterion is evaluated against the effective applicability policy; if selected it runs exactly once in Round A, while disabled/non-applicable criteria run zero times with provenance. The implementation story must name this as an intentional reversal of 761e, not a compatibility-preserving refactor.

New executable defect: `.joe-janitor/rp06-failure-checkpoint-probe.py` injected one non-systemic ordinary Pass-1 criterion failure, then reran identical material with a healthy runner. First run: 1 failed model call, findings empty, `chunk_errors` absent, and checkpoint payload `[]`. Second run: `chunks_resumed=1`, healthy calls=0, findings empty. Root: `sizing.pass1_with_ladder` converts non-context exceptions to `([], calls)` before the outer failure counter; `_chunk` then persists that empty value as a completed checkpoint. A transient failure is consequently replayed as `succeeded(clean)` indefinitely until material changes.

Required shared-executor invariant: `failed` is distinct from `succeeded` with zero findings; failed/cancelled/shed units never write success checkpoints; consumed usage/failure classification survive; failed units retry next run. This changes replay/cost behavior explicitly but does not itself settle the current-run final-verdict policy.

Decision-ready RP-06 queue is now: (D6.1) parity-first current-run failure projection versus posture-aware normalization; (D6.2) honor explicit code-review `usd_budget` during cutover versus journal-only shadowing first; (D6.3) preserve existing per-gate scheduler/cache modes during cutover versus activating code-review parallelism/checkpoints. Recommendation: typed/correct checkpoint outcomes immediately, parity-first gate verdicts and scheduling for the structural slice, explicit-budget enforcement because the authored request field should be truthful.

Prior art independently rechecked at current upstream heads: ansible-lint `8824f98d49` shares typed rule selection/execution/results while rules own matching; Semgrep `808ee51cda` returns typed findings plus structured errors, then applies suppression and exit policy separately. Full note: `.joe-janitor/rp06-chronology-failure-critique.md`.

## Context / Problem
The recovered 2026-08-16 janitor plan contains approved-but-lossy RP-02 through RP-06 decisions. Before these items become implementation stories, the maintainer needs evidence-backed discussions that preserve prior architectural intent, cover hard-won bug and test behavior, and resolve implementation-critical ambiguities. Durable recovery authority is the closed tracker record `irascible-clueless-basenji` (`ee98-a2c0-7d12-4c75`), whose description and comments record the recovered RP definitions and evidence. The checkout-local `.joe-janitor/report-2026-08-16-recovered.md` is an operator-supplied ignored working copy; if it is absent in another checkout, the durable ticket plus the source/ADR/test/ticket citations it names are sufficient to reconstruct it.

## Approach
Research each RP independently against current source, focused behavioral tests, ticket/ADR/commit history, and relevant maintained-project prior art. Record a decision-ready brief per RP under the checkout-local `.joe-janitor/` archive, with the situation, intended end state, invariants versus intentional behavior changes, edge/failure scenarios, concrete implementation seams, migration/rollback considerations, and remaining maintainer-only decisions. Use read-only or checkout-local probes where framework behavior is uncertain. This fits the janitor approval phase because it reduces ambiguity without editing production code or prematurely creating implementation stories.

## Scope
No tracked repository file changes. Read-only scope includes `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`, `src/rebar/_cli/`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/`, their focused tests, `docs/adr/`, exact historical tickets/commits, and the durable recovery ticket. Outputs live in checkout-local ignored `.joe-janitor/rp02-*.md` through `.joe-janitor/rp06-*.md` when available and in durable comments on this ticket.

## Verification
This is an investigation task. Evidence crosses source boundaries through focused existing tests and narrowly scoped checkout-local probes. The oracles are exact current outcomes, failure modes, ownership boundaries, call/reference inventories, and cited historical decisions. Any behavior change is labeled as a maintainer decision rather than silently treated as an invariant. Each local brief is read back and summarized durably on this ticket; the ticket summary is the portable completion record when ignored artifacts are unavailable to an attested reviewer.
